Scope: spec `pose-review-conclude-ignores-unrelated-local-edits` (R1–R3, decision D1). Three times in one session `pose review conclude --apply` refused a changes-requested run because the implementer was already editing the sealed subject for the next round ("persisted review inputs no longer materialize: sealed bytes changed"), and it wrote a permanent refusal record that had to be deleted by hand.
- R1: currency (the bundle is the current subject; sealed inputs still materialize from the working tree) now matters only to an approval. `reviewConclusionChecks` keeps the run-record integrity check; `reviewConclusionCurrency` runs only when the draft approves. The run proof of a completed run whose draft does not approve needs `ReviewRunRecordStands`, not `ReviewRunStillGoverns` (`runProofContextConflict`). The provenance check re-renders a run's brief from its bundle without requiring it to be current (`renderRunBriefMatching`); handoff and resume keep requiring it.
- R2: an approval refused only for currency returns its reasons with "not recorded" and writes no conclusion record.
- R3: `TestARequestForChangesConcludesOverLocalEdits`, `TestAnApprovalOverLocalEditsIsNotRecordedAndConcludesLater`. Each change failed its test when mutated out.

Please check in particular that nothing can turn a non-approving verdict of a stale bundle into an approval of the current one, and that closeout and verification still read only the current bundle.

Draft format rules, enforced by the conclusion preflight:
- New findings use short unprefixed IDs (N1, N2, …). Round-prefixed IDs go only in `prior_findings`, and only for the findings the brief lists under "Findings to account for", with exactly id, status and evidence.
- Structural-delta mappings go inside the criterion that answers them, with `basis` set to a requirement or a decision of this spec (R1–R3, D1).
- A criterion scoped to a component cites evidence from that component only.

Sandbox limits: the checkout is sealed and read-only. Never `cd`; keep the checkout root as the working directory. Keep test runs focused (`go -C pose-mcp test ./internal/pose -run 'OverLocalEdits|ConcludeReviewRun|RunProof|Provenance|Handoff|Continuity'`). A tool you cannot rerun in the sandbox is a limit of the run, not a defect of the subject: cite the sealed evidence that covers it, then decide on the code itself.
